uncited: Frequency-Domain Methods represent volumetric data (including dynamic 4D spacetime volumes) as a superposition of basis functions in the frequency domain, often utilizing tensor decomposition to reduce memory usage.
Unlike spatial-domain methods that store values at grid points, this approach stores spectral coefficients.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Fourier Projection-Slice Volume Rendering](824-fourier-projection-slice-volume-rendering.md) by focusing on explicit spectral representation and decomposition for compact storage rather than projection-slice extraction for rendering, and from [DCT-based Volume Rendering](5396-dct-based-volume-rendering.md) by using complex exponential Fourier bases instead of discrete cosine bases.
*   **Output:** A set of decomposed vectors (or tensors) representing the frequency coefficients, allowing reconstruction of the field value at any coordinate.
The method replaces the dense 4D frequency volume $\tilde{\mathbf{D}}(u, v, w, k)$ with a set of low-rank factors using CANDECOMP/PARAFAC (CP) decomposition.
*   $\tilde{\mathbf{v}}^K \in \mathbb{C}^{K \times R}$: Vectors corresponding to the $t$-axis (time) frequency bins $k=1 \dots K$.
*   **Positional Encoding (Optional):** A function $f(t)$ used to parameterize time-dependent features, defined as $f(t) = [1, \sin(t), \cos(t), \sin(2t), \cos(2t), \dots]$.
**Global Transformation (Implicit):** The input volume is conceptually transformed into the frequency domain.
**Evaluation:** To compute the value at a specific spacetime point $(x, y, z, t)$, the inner products of the positional encodings (if used) and the decomposed vectors are calculated.
*   **Training Tricks:** Weighted L1 loss is applied to regularize the decomposed vectors, assigning higher weights to high-frequency coefficients to maintain smoothness.
*   **Strengths:** Compact representation for dynamic 4D scenes; enables differentiable rendering via spectral coefficients.
*   **When to use:** When memory is constrained for 4D dynamic volumes and high-frequency detail is less critical than compact storage.
*   **When not to use:** When real-time interactive performance or high-fidelity static rendering is required.
It was explored as an orthogonal approach to spatial decomposition, leveraging Fourier Theory to represent spacetime values.
